power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

text.text: Introduction: This study psychometrically refined the Cognitive Assessment of Older Adults in Music Therapy (ACPIM) and evaluated its convergent validity and longitudinal stability relative to the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA).
Method: Participants included 180 institutionalized older adults (mean age = 79.0 ± 8.2 years; 93.9% cognitively impaired).
Psychometric refinement integrated Network Psychometrics, Rasch Partial Credit Modeling, and Confirmatory Factor Analysis.
Results: MoCA items required category collapsing to resolve disordered thresholds.

Refinement yielded a unidimensional 5-item scale (ACPIM-5) demonstrating adequate fit (χ²(4) = 4.039, p = 0.401; CFI = 1.000; TLI = 1.000; RMSEA = 0.007, 90% CI [0.000, 0.113]; ω = 0.896) and high fidelity with the 18-item version (r = 0.930).
A bifactor model confirmed to be a dominant General Factor (H = 0.896; factor determinacy = 0.928) convergent with the MoCA (r = 0.380).
ROC analysis demonstrated acceptable preliminary discrimination (AUC = 0.768, 95% CI [0.593, 0.943]; cutoff = 12.5; sensitivity = 72.8%; specificity = 81.8%).
Discussion: The ACPIM-5 satisfied 7-day metric invariance (Δχ²(5) = 3.418, p = 0.636), confirming factor loading equivalence.
In contrast, the MoCA violated scalar invariance (Δχ²(20) = 43.896, p = 0.0015), indicating threshold drift.

text.text: Integrating network psychometrics-specifically Unique Variable Analysis To address these research aims, we formulated four a priori hypotheses: H1.
Structural refinement: Removing topological redundancies will yield a parsimonious, unidimensional short-form version characterized by ordered response thresholds and adequate construct fit; H2.

Convergent validity: Preserved cognitive performance observed during music therapy will demonstrate a moderate, statistically significant positive correlation with performance on the clinical gold standard, reflecting a shared underlying continuum of neurocognitive functioning; H3.
Diagnostic accuracy: The refined observational score will demonstrate acceptable discriminative capacity in screening for cognitive decline relative to the established MoCA clinical cutoff; H4.

Temporal stability: The ACPIM-5 will exhibit longitudinal measurement invariance and high test-retest reliability across a 7-day interval, reflecting stable observational scoring under routine clinical conditions.

Method Participants and Eligibility Criteria ACPIM-5 The sample comprised 180 older adults recruited across 12 public and private LTCFs for the Elderly in Curitiba and its Metropolitan Region, Paraná, Brazil.

Inclusion criteria were: (a) age 60 years or older; (b) residing in one of the participating LTCFs; and (c) active participation in a structured group MT program for at least three consecutive months.

Exclusion criteria included severe, uncorrected sensory (auditory or visual) impairments that precluded participation in musical activities or paper-andpencil testing; active medical instability; or and incomplete clinical records.

The mean age of the participants was 79.0 ± 8.2 years (range: 60-101 years), with a predominance of females (67.8%, n = 122), widowed individuals (41.7%, n = 75), and participants with elementary education (57.8%, n = 104).

Longitudinal Measurement Invariance and Retest Stability Hierarchical invariance testing across the 7-day interval supported configural invariance for the ACPIM-5 (Table 2; χ²(29) = 30.098, p = 0.409; CFI = 1.000; RMSEA = 0.015, 90% CI [0.000, 0.060]).
Metric invariance was confirmed, as constraining factor loadings across time did not significantly worsen model fit compared to the configural model (Δχ²(5) = 3.418, p = 0.636).

When attempting to constrain item thresholds the model encountered empirical under-identification and asymptotic singularity resulting from near-unity test-retest item correlations across the 7-day ACPIM-5 interval (item 12 autocorrelation r ≈ 1.0), which produced a non-positive definite covariance matrix.
Consequently, metric invariance was retained as the most parsimonious and tenable measurement model, demonstrating equivalent measurement units across repeated assessments.
Latent trait reliability remained highly consistent across both assessment waves (ωT1 = 0.920; ωT2 = 0.917).

For the MoCA, while metric invariance was supported (Δχ²(7) = 8.746, p = 0.271), full scalar threshold invariance was significantly rejected across the same 7-day window (Δχ²(20) = 43.896, p = 0.0015), indicating significant threshold drift across repeated administrations.

The baseline MoCA initial poor approximation fit and the presence of disordered transition thresholds across items 3 (Attention), 6 (Memory), and 7 (Orientation) underscore the structural limitations of conventional paper-and-pencil screening in institutionalized senescence.

text.text: In this context, ACPIM-5 abstract symbolic tasks such as cube copying or serial sevens lose discriminative precision, producing extreme floor clustering around a mean of 15.7 points-well below the conventional 26-point threshold.
The category consolidation performed in this study recalibrated the MoCA metric to reflect the clinical realities of institutionalized elders.

Collapsing categories 0 and 1 in Visuospatial and Memory domains indicates that, for severely dependent older adults, total failure and partial failure represent functionally equivalent manifestations of exhausted cognitive reserve.

Similarly, reducing Orientation from seven discrete levels to three functional tiers (severe disorientation, moderate disorientation, and preserved orientation) successfully restored monotonic threshold progression.

These adjustments demonstrate that while the recalibrated MoCA remains a robust diagnostic benchmark, its reliance on formal graphomotor execution and explicit evaluative settings underscores the clinical utility of complementary, ecologically grounded observational tools such as the ACPIM-5.

Furthermore, the near-unity correlation observed between the raw sum score of the ACPIM-5 and its latent trait parameter confirms that clinicians can reliably implement the simple 0-to-20 summation in routine practice as a direct, unmediated proxy of the individual's latent neurocognitive functioning.

From a neurocognitive perspective, reproducing a melodic phrase (ACPIM's item 12) requires complex auditory-motor translation, vocal-motor planning, and working memory maintenance supported by frontoparietal and superior temporal networks-systems that suffer early degradation in progressive dementias (Leggieri et al., 2019; Thaut & Hömberg, 2014).

text.text: In sharp contrast, musical memory (Item 7) and concentration (Item 2) operated as foundational baseline anchors, successfully ACPIM-5 differentiating older adults even at severe stages of cognitive decline.

The relative ease and diagnostic stability of these items corroborate the musical memory reserve hypothesis (Albuquerque et al., 2012; Maseda et al., 2018), showing that neural pathways supporting familiar melodic recognition remain preserved long after declarative memory networks collapse.

text.text: The sequential pruning process eliminated critical measurement artifacts common in clinician-rated observational scales.
In geriatric observational settings, extreme multicollinearity and inflated initial reliability coefficients, such as ω = 1.035, typically signal severe local dependence.

A plausible behavioral explanation for this artifact is rater familiarity and potential halo effects (Cooper, 1981), where a global clinical impression of overall impairment leads clinicians to assign uniform ratings across disparate items.

text.text: From a clinical standpoint, the near-collinear association between item pairs 3-4 (ρ = 0.98) and 8-9 (ρ = 0.97) probably reveals behavioral synonymy, due the fact that, during active group music making, clinicians cannot realistically differentiate sustained visual focus from auditory engagement, or melodic anticipation from structural recognition.
These behaviors co-occur in real time, making separate rating categories functionally indistinguishable.

Similarly, the overfit observed in items 8 and 11 reflects that, once an older adult demonstrates basic communicative engagement, music therapists systematically award top scores to these items, eliminating meaningful variance.
Conversely, the severe underfit of Item 16 ("intention to improvise") highlights the hazard of rating inferred internal states rather than discrete observable actions.

In severe dementia, discerning whether an atypical musical response reflects deliberate creative intent or involuntary ACPIM-5 motor perseveration is highly subjective, introducing substantial unmodeled noise (Fachner, 2016).
text.formatted: In severe dementia, discerning whether an atypical musical response reflects deliberate creative intent or involuntary ACPIM-5 motor perseveration is highly subjective, introducing substantial unmodeled noise <ref type="bibr" target="#b12">(Fachner, 2016)</ref>.

text.text: From a clinical and psychometric perspective, the exclusion of items 4, 9, and 10 was warranted because they clustered at similar difficulty parameters alongside Item 2 (-0.033 to 0.541 logits).

In geriatric MT, sustained concentration (Item 2), motor initiative to play or sing (Item 4), entrainment to the music therapist's song (Item 9), and articulation of familiar lyrics (Item 10) represent a shared plateau of baseline sensorimotor reactivity (Arruda, 2022; Thaut & Hömberg, 2014).

text.text: In institutionalized older adults with moderate neurodegenerative decline, these behaviors co-occur, for instance: following the melodic lead of the music therapist inherently demands sustained attention and basic verbal articulation of overlearned songs.
In IRT, maintaining clustered items targeting the exact same latent trait locus generates redundant test information without extending measurement range (Bond & Fox, 2015; Smith, 2002).

text.text: Retaining Item 2 as the single, psychometrically optimal anchor for this ability interval achieved structural parsimony and alleviated clinician assessment burden without sacrificing diagnostic sensitivity.

The robust emergence of the General Factor (G)-characterized by high construct replicability and factor determinacy-demonstrates that structured musical engagement and standardized clinical instruments draw upon a common architecture of global neurocognitive integrity.

The substantial attenuation of subscale unique reliability once global variance was accounted for indicates that in institutionalized older adults, cognitive reserve operates as a unified, systemic capacity rather than fragmented modular silos.
The direct latent path between instruments was statistically significant, accompanied by a moderate factor score correlation.
This pattern indicates that while the ACPIM-5 shares an underlying neurocognitive substrate with the MoCA, approximately 73% to 85% of its variance is distinct.
This moderate convergence highlights meaningful differences in assessment modality and cognitive demands.

Because musical engagement recruits resilient sensorimotor networks and implicit processing that persist even in advanced decline (Albuquerque et al., 2012; Stern, 2009), the ACPIM-5 serves as a complementary, context grounded metric that captures preserved operational capacity in populations where traditional tests encounter severe floor effects.

text.text: ROC curve analysis supported the practical utility of the ACPIM-5 as an observational screening tool (AUC = 0.768, 95% CI [0.593, 0.943]).

The identification of an optimal empirical cutoff of 12.5 points established a balanced diagnostic profile, yielding 72.8% sensitivity and 81.8% specificity relative to the standard MoCA benchmark (< 26 points).

text.text: Methodologically, the clinical interpretation of the ROC parameters must be contextualized within the high-dependency profile of long-term care facilities.

With 93.9% of residents presenting objective impairment (MoCA < 26), the control subgroup was inherently limited (n = 11), leading to wide confidence intervals for both the AUC (95% CI [0.593, 0.943]) and specificity (95% CI [52.3%, 94.9%]).

text.text: Although the empirical cutoff of 12.5 points achieved a balanced sensitivity and point-estimate specificity, the substantial uncertainty at the lower boundary of discrimination indicates that the ACPIM-5 functions as an initial observational screener rather than a definitive diagnostic test.
In practical care routines, a score below 13 points serves as a clinical flag for preserved functional decline, signaling the need for multidisciplinary attention.

However, due to the severe institutional floor clustering on the standard 26-point MoCA cutoff, future studies should evaluate the ACPIM-5 against stratified thresholds adapted to low educational strata and advanced dementia staging (e.g., MoCA < 15 or functional staging tools such as the clinical dementia rating scales) to determine its discriminative precision across intermediate stages of neurodegeneration.

text.text: The ACPIM-5 demonstrated full metric invariance, establishing that the factor loadings and measurement units remain equivalent across consecutive sessions.

Although the full scalar model could not be formally estimated due to empirical singularity caused by high short-term stability, the confirmation of metric invariance ensures that score changes over time reflect shifts in the underlying latent construct rather than alterations in scale calibration.
In contrast, the MoCA significantly violated scalar threshold invariance across the same 7-day window.

This threshold drift illustrates a recognized vulnerability of traditional direct cognitive screening batteries as immediate re-administration induces practice effects and familiarity reactivity, thereby altering item difficulty parameters.

Conversely, an observational assessment conducted during active music therapy evaluates real-time functional behaviors in an ecological setting, reducing the patient's exposure to explicit evaluative stress and direct task memorization artifacts.
First, the sample comprised exclusively institutionalized older adults residing in LTCFs, of whom 93.9% exhibited objective cognitive impairment according to standard MoCA criteria.

Consequently, the cognitively preserved subgroup was small, which ACPIM-5 substantially reduced statistical power for the ROC estimation and produced wide confidence intervals for both the AUC and specificity.
While this sample faithfully reflects the clinical reality of Brazilian LTCFs, where severe impairment is ubiquitous, the 12.5 cutoff must be treated as preliminary.
It cannot be generalized to communitydwelling cohorts without prior recalibration, as ceiling effects may emerge in higherfunctioning populations.
Future studies should replicate this validation in community health centers and adult day-care cohorts with a more balanced distribution of cognitive stages.

Second, although the 7-day retest interval was methodologically optimal for isolating measurement stability and testing invariance without biological disease progression, it precluded an evaluation of the scale's sensitivity to longitudinal change over extended clinical interventions.

Longitudinal randomized controlled trials spanning 6 to 12 months are necessary to determine whether the ACPIM-5 can detect subtle, intervention-induced neurocognitive stabilization or improvement in response to systematic MT.
Third, while the sequential pruning process effectively resolved empirical item redundancy, the ACPIM-5 remains an observational rating instrument completed by the attending music therapist.

Because the same clinician evaluated the residents at both baseline and the 7-day retest, and inter-rater reliability was not formally examined in this trial, the observed temporal stability may partially reflect rater consistency and carryover memory rather than pure latent trait invariance.
Future studies should implement blind, independent dual-rater designs and video-based ratings to establish inter-examiner concordance across distinct clinical settings.
The psychometric refinement conducted in this study successfully transformed an 18-item observational protocol into a parsimonious, psychometrically robust 5-item screening instrument.

The ACPIM-5 demonstrates that systematic clinical observation of musical behavior taps into Global Cognitive Functioning, providing a context grounded screening tool that moderately converges with standardized clinical batteries while offering practical feasibility in music therapeutic settings.

Supported by 7-day metric invariance and an empirical screening cutoff of 12.5 points, the ACPIM-5 provides multidisciplinary teams with an efficient, rapid, and ecologically grounded tool for routine cognitive monitoring in institutionalized dementia care.
Ultimately, this study supports an ecological shift in cognitive assessment, demonstrating that real-time expressive engagement during MT reflects preserved neurocognitive reserve.
The ACPIM-5 emerges as an efficient, rapid, and structurally validated tool for routine clinical monitoring and functional cognitive screening in longterm geriatric care.
